problem:
Let $u=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ and $v=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$ Find the vector projection of $u$ onto $v.$

${\text{proj}}_{v}\,u=⟨$
{{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}$,$
{{field-3}}
$⟩$
worked_solution:
Using the formula for the vector projection, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{v}\,u & =\frac{u\cdot v}{v\cdot v}v \\  & =\frac{{u}_{x}{v}_{x}+{u}_{y}{v}_{y}+{u}_{z}{v}_{z}}{{v}_{x}^{2}+{v}_{y}^{2}+{v}_{z}^{2}}v \\  & =\frac{(1)\cdot 2+(-2)\cdot 1+(1)\cdot 0}{{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}}v \\  & =\frac{0}{5}v \\  & =⟨\,0,0,0\,⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
